record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: If A is an integral matrix in CP_n, meaning a real symmetric n x n matrix with integer entries and A = B B^T for some entrywise nonnegative B, must A have a rational completely positive factorization? Equivalently, must A admit a representation A = sum_i alpha_i b_i b_i^T in which every alpha_i is rational and every vector b_i has rational entries?

evidence.quote: Given a matrix A ∈ CPn all of whose entries are integral, does A always have a rational cp-factorization?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S_n(\mathbb{R})$ denote the set of real symmetric $n\times n$ matrices. A matrix $A\in S_n(\mathbb{R})$ is called completely positive if there exists an entrywise nonnegative (not necessarily square) real matrix $B$ with $A = BB^{T}$; equivalently, $A$ admits a representation
$$A = \sum_{i=1}^{k} \alpha_i\, b_i b_i^{T},$$
for some integer $k\ge 1$, with $\alpha_i\ge 0$ and $b_i\in\mathbb{R}^n_{\ge 0}$. Denote the cone of all such matrices by $\mathrm{CP}_n$.

A rational cp-factorization of $A$ is a representation
$$A = \sum_{i=1}^{k} \alpha_i\, b_i b_i^{T},$$
in which every coefficient $\alpha_i\in\mathbb{Q}_{\ge 0}$ and every vector $b_i\in\mathbb{Q}^n_{\ge 0}$.

Question: Suppose $A\in\mathrm{CP}_n$ has all entries in $\mathbb{Z}$. Must $A$ admit a rational cp-factorization?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether every integral (or even every rational) matrix in $\mathrm{CP}_n$ admits a rational cp-factorization remains open in general. Partial results are known: every rational matrix in the interior of $\mathrm{CP}_n$ has a rational cp-factorization, and every integral $2\times 2$ completely positive matrix admits even an integral cp-factorization. Boundary cases are still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Completely Positive Matrices: Real, Rational, and Integral
status_evidence.snippet: Every integral completely positive 2x2 matrix has an integral cp-factorization; whether every rational completely positive matrix has a rational cp-factorization remains open.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is still open in general; partial results exist (interior matrices and 2x2 integral case).

status_evidence.title: A simplex algorithm for rational cp-factorization
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm producing rational cp-factorizations in cases where they exist; existence in full generality not established.
status_evidence.claim: Algorithmic progress, but general existence remains unresolved.
